item.title: China wants human-like AI systems to have socialist values
item.description: China is tightening rules for human-like AI, requiring service providers to inform users when they are interacting with AI. Systems designed to mimic humans must undergo security and ethical reviews, adhering to socialist values and avoiding content that threatens national security.

item.title: BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman enlists as Bangladesh voter
item.description: Tarique Rahman, son of former PM Khaleda Zia, has completed voter registration and obtained a national identity card. This marks his return after 17 years in self-exile. Rahman will now contest the upcoming parliamentary polls on February 12. He is set to represent his ancestral Bogura Sadar constituency. This is his first electoral contest.

item.title: FBI's finally moving out of historic HQ
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel announced the permanent closure of the agency's aging J. Edgar Hoover headquarters, relocating personnel to the former US Agency for International Development building. This move, after decades of planning, aims to save taxpayer funds and provide a modern facility. The decision is a setback for Maryland, which was previously promised the new headquarters.

item.title: Bangladesh unrest: 'Some part' of Yunus-led govt allowed attacks on newspapers
item.description: Editors' Council president Nurul Kabir stated that a segment of the interim government permitted the vandalism of Prothom Alo, The Daily Star, and Chhayanaut following radical leader Sharif Osman Hadi's death. These attacks followed prior announcements, with arrests revealing clear political affiliations, raising concerns about the government's inaction.

item.title: Bangladesh: Mob attacks singer's concert; 25 hurt
item.description: A concert featuring popular Bangladeshi singer James in Faridpur was attacked by a mob, injuring over 25 people, mostly students. Organizers' mismanagement and failure to anticipate the crowd size led to the chaos. This incident reinforces concerns about growing insecurity for artistes in Bangladesh.

item.title: Despite crackdown on activism, US techies go on picking fights
item.description: Tech workers are increasingly organizing and advocating for better conditions amidst widespread layoffs and a shift towards AI investment. Despite crackdowns, activism persists, with employees at companies like Kickstarter and Google pushing for improved job security and fair treatment. This trend reflects a changing perception of tech roles, moving beyond individualistic professional identities to collective action.
item.dc:creator: Noam Scheiber

item.title: 'If Ukraine did not want to resolve ...': Putin sends warning ahead of Trump-Zelenskyy meeting
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin declared Russia will achieve its military goals by force if Ukraine avoids peaceful resolution. This comes after Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiy accused Russia of wanting to continue the war. Russian commanders reported capturing several towns in Ukraine's Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia regions to President Putin.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Empty childcare centres and millions paid: YouTuber Nick Shirley's investigation sparks outrage over alleged Minnesota welfare fraud
item.description: A viral investigation by YouTuber Nick Shirley alleges up to $8 billion in Minnesota taxpayer funds may have been lost to massive welfare fraud. The probe highlights empty childcare centers and numerous healthcare businesses receiving substantial public money with little apparent operation. The claims have sparked outrage, demanding accountability from state agencies and officials.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: School uniforms, binoculars and more: Jeffrey Epstein’s Amazon purchases revealed in DOJ files
item.description: Newly revealed US Department of Justice documents expose Jeffrey Epstein's disturbing Amazon shopping history, featuring schoolgirl uniforms and sexual aids. Experts view these purchases, including items like a prostate massager and books like 'Lolita,' as indicative of his predatory behavior, reflecting coercion and a drive for domination. The ongoing release of records continues to illuminate the disgraced financier's actions.

item.title: ‘How are you stranded in your own country?’ MAGA mocks as H-1B visa holders stranded by stamping delays
item.description: MAGA figures and commentators are expressing satisfaction with India's H-1B visa stamping delays, with some mocking the situation. Hundreds of Indian H-1B visa holders are stranded in India, facing rescheduled appointments until 2026, preventing their return to the US and creating employment uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Racist and it ... ': Podcaster Brad Polumbo slams Nick Fuentes for attack on 'anchor baby' Indian-origin Republican Vivek Ramaswamy
item.description: Podcaster Brad Polumbo has labeled far-right extremist Nick Fuentes as racist for attacking Indian-origin Republican Vivek Ramaswamy. Fuentes urged people not to vote for Ramaswamy, suggesting he should "go back to India." Polumbo criticized Fuentes's stance, highlighting his opposition to Ramaswamy based on race and faith, despite Ramaswamy's alignment with Republican values.

item.title: Meet Jayshree Ullal: Indian-origin billionaire at the top of Hurun's rich list
item.description: Jayshree Ullal, CEO of Arista Networks, leads India's richest tech executives for 2025. She has surpassed Sundar Pichai and Satya Nadella. Ullal's net worth is $5.7 billion. item.title: Mora Namdar's net worth, education and love life: What to know about Trump's new Secretary for Consular Affairs
item.description: Mora Namdar, an Iranian-American lawyer and beauty salon owner, takes on a key role in the Trump administration. She will now lead the Bureau of Consular Affairs, overseeing vital services like visas and passports. Namdar's appointment follows her previous roles within the State Department and the US Agency for Global Media.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why Will Byers’ gay confession has MAGA viewers fuming and Stranger Things fans split
item.description: Stranger Things' final season faced backlash for Will Byers' coming-out scene, criticized for its timing and perceived narrative interruption. While some defended it as crucial for Will's character arc and weakening Vecna, many viewers felt it stalled the apocalypse for a monologue they already understood, leading to accusations of forced messaging.

item.title: Why is Adin Ross claiming Hasan “HasanAbi” Piker killed his own pet dog? Kick streamer’s livestream allegations go viral
item.description: Kick streamer Adin Ross has leveled serious accusations against Twitch streamer Hasan “HasanAbi” Piker, alleging he killed his own former pet dog, Fish. Ross claimed HasanAbi was responsible for the dog's death and suggested disturbing behavior, despite HasanAbi explaining the situation as an old, out-of-context clip where his dog died during COVID.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Clavicular breaks silence with self-defense claim following disturbing Cybertruck livestream moment
item.description: A controversial livestream featuring streamer Clavicular has sparked outrage after footage showed his Tesla Cybertruck moving forward with a person on its hood on Christmas Eve. Clavicular claims fear drove his actions, alleging he believed individuals surrounding his vehicle were armed. The incident has raised serious questions about online accountability and real-world danger.
